title: Radio: IP-1 Barn 3 Power Loss

fields.centerName: Calder County EOC, Public Safety Building Training Room

lines.text: EOC, IP-1 site. Priority traffic for Operations.

Barn 3 lost power at 09:52. The pole transformer on the north service drop blew. Lights are out, and all twelve tunnel fans and the water pump on that panel are down. About fifteen thousand five hundred toms are in there. Barn temp went from fifty-eight to sixty-six degrees in six minutes, and the ammonia at the door reads thirty-one ppm and it's climbing. The electric co-op dispatcher says a line crew is about four hours out.

EOC, IP-1 Safety, same location. The barn's electrician says your two thirty-kilowatt county generators together would carry the lights and about eight of the twelve fans. We've got no water to the drinker lines in barn 3, and the depop team says it needs water on site whichever method command picks. Who's sending what, and who on site is in charge of it when it gets here? Over.

fields.voiceStyle: First speaker: middle-aged male farm manager, tense, talking fast over idling equipment. Second speaker: calm, clipped female safety officer, deliberate and businesslike.

instructorNote: This tests whether Ops sends both 30 kW county generators, with a Highway Department operator, and the Larkin Fire District 4,000-gallon tanker by the 230th Street lane, since the CR 12 bridge is posted at 10 tons. Watch that Ops says state/APHIS incident command directs how the equipment is used on site while the county delivers, fuels and maintains it, that county operators get PPE and symptom checks, and that someone notices the tanker can't also cover the staging-area water role.
